description: ClickHouse cluster admin dashboard — on-call incident response. Default time range: 6h.
title: ClickHouse Admin

panels.title: Active Errors — system.errors
panels.description: Active errors from system.errors across all nodes, sorted by most recent. Empty table = no active errors — cluster is healthy.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT name AS error, last_error_message AS message, value AS count, toDateTime(last_error_time) AS last_seen FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.errors) WHERE value > 0 ORDER BY last_error_time DESC LIMIT 30
SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards = 1

panels.title: CPU Usage — per Pod
panels.description: CPU utilisation as a fraction of all available vCPUs (0–100%). OSUserTime + OSSystemTime report CPU-seconds/wall-second; dividing by OSNumVirtualCPUs normalises to a proper percentage.

targets.expr:
(
  sum by (pod)({__name__=~"ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_OSUserTimeCPU.*", cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"})
  + sum by (pod)({__name__=~"ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_OSSystemTimeCPU.*", cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"})
) / on(pod) group_left()
count by (pod)({__name__=~"ClickHouseAsyncMetrics_OSUserTimeCPU.*", cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: RAM Usage — per Pod
panels.description: Memory explicitly tracked by the ClickHouse allocator per pod. Actual RSS may be slightly higher. A rising trend without matching query load indicates a memory leak.

panels.title: Network I/O — per Pod (RX=Inbound, TX=Outbound)
panels.description: RX (Receive) = bytes incoming to the pod. TX (Transmit) = bytes sent out. Imbalance signals hot-spotting or a misconfigured load balancer.

panels.title: Storage Used (Hot) — per Pod
panels.description: Hot storage used per replica. Replicas on the same shard should be nearly equal — divergence indicates one replica has more/fewer merged parts, or TTL moves ran on only some nodes. If the gap grows over time, check merge lag and replication queue depth.

panels.title: Failed Queries/sec — per Pod
panels.description: Rate of failed queries per pod. A spike on one pod while others are stable points to a bad replica or OOM.

panels.title: Insert Throughput — per Table
panels.description: Rows/sec per table from system.query_log.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfInterval(event_time, INTERVAL $__interval_s second) AS time, tables[1] AS table, sum(written_rows) / $__interval_s AS rows_per_sec FROM system.query_log WHERE event_time >= toDateTime(intDiv($__from, 1000)) AND event_time <= toDateTime(intDiv($__to, 1000)) AND type = 'QueryFinish' AND query_kind = 'Insert' AND length(tables) > 0 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY time, table ORDER BY time ASC

panels.title: Insert Throughput — per Replica (Pod)
panels.description: INSERT rows per second per pod from the Prometheus exporter. Compare with the per-table panel to identify which tables drive insert load.

panels.title: Active Parts — per Table (Current Snapshot)
panels.description: Current part count per table. High part counts indicate merge lag.

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, count() AS active_parts, sum(rows) AS total_rows, formatReadableSize(sum(bytes_on_disk)) AS size_on_disk, max(modification_time) AS last_modified FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY database, table ORDER BY active_parts DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: Async Insert — Pending Queue Depth
panels.description: Pending async inserts buffered server-side. A growing queue risks data loss if the server restarts.

panels.title: INSERT Queries per Second
panels.description: Number of INSERT queries per second per pod.

panels.title: Average INSERT Latency — per Pod

targets.expr: sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_InsertQueryTimeMicroseconds{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_InsertQuery{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / 1000

panels.description: Average INSERT query duration in milliseconds per pod. Spikes here while INSERT QPS is stable suggest large batches or resource contention.

panels.title: Async Insert — Batch Size (Rows per Flush)
panels.description: Average number of rows batched per async insert flush. A low value (< 100) means clients are sending tiny inserts and async batching is not effective.

panels.title: Parts Created per Second — per Pod
panels.description: Rate of new MergeTree parts written to disk due to INSERT operations per pod. High rates mean inserts are arriving faster than merges can consolidate — watch Active Parts.

panels.title: Query Latency (avg) — per Pod
panels.description: Average query duration in ms. ClickHouse does not expose latency histograms via Prometheus; p99 requires system.query_log.

targets.expr: sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_QueryTimeMicroseconds{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_Query{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / 1000

panels.title: Queries per Second (Total)
panels.description: Total queries per second per pod (all types: SELECT, INSERT, mutations, etc.).

panels.title: SELECT Queries per Second
panels.description: SELECT queries per second per pod.

panels.title: Average SELECT Latency — per Pod

targets.expr: sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_SelectQueryTimeMicroseconds{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_SelectQuery{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])) / 1000

panels.description: Average SELECT query duration in milliseconds per pod.

panels.title: Active Background Merges — per Pod
panels.description: Number of active background merge/mutation tasks per pod. Compare with Merge Pool Saturation to see whether the pool is full.

panels.title: Merge Pool Saturation
panels.description: Active merges vs pool size (left axis). Saturation % on right axis. When saturation reaches 100% and part count is rising, merges cannot keep pace with inserts.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (pod)(ClickHouseMetrics_BackgroundMergesAndMutationsPoolTask{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}) / sum by (pod)(ClickHouseMetrics_BackgroundMergesAndMutationsPoolSize{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"})

panels.title: Async Insert Buffered Flushes/sec
panels.description: Rate of async insert buffer flushes to disk. High flush rate means many small insert batches.

panels.title: Replication Queue Depth — per Replica
panels.description: Pending replication tasks per replica. Empty = no backlog (healthy). A growing queue on one replica indicates it is falling behind.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    hostName() AS replica,
    database,
    table,
    count() AS queue_depth
FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.replication_queue)
GROUP BY replica, database, table
ORDER BY queue_depth DESC
LIMIT 50
SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards = 1

panels.title: Replication Lag — per Pod (over time)
panels.description: Maximum absolute replication delay across all replicated tables per pod. 0 = fully in sync. Persistent lag above a few seconds indicates the replica cannot keep up with inserts.

panels.title: S3 Storage Used
panels.description: Total bytes in S3 tiered storage. Adjust 's3' in metric name to match your S3 disk name.

panels.title: S3 Write Throughput
panels.description: Total bytes written to S3 per second per pod.

panels.title: S3 Read Throughput
panels.description: Total bytes read from S3 per second per pod (all sources: user SELECT, merges, etc.).

panels.title: S3 GET Operations/sec
panels.description: S3 GET request rate per pod. Use the 'S3 GET Attribution' table below to break down by source (user queries, merges, TTL).

panels.title: S3 Merge Reads (bytes/sec)
panels.description: Bytes read from S3 by background merges on tiered data.

panels.title: S3 GET Attribution — by Source (selected time range)
panels.description: Breaks down S3 GET requests by what triggered them: user SELECT queries, merges/OPTIMIZE, TTL moves, or other internals.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT multiIf(query_kind = 'Select', 'User SELECT', query_kind = 'Insert', 'INSERT', match(lower(query), 'optimize|merge'), 'Merge / OPTIMIZE', match(lower(query), 'ttl'), 'TTL', 'Other') AS source, count() AS query_count, sum(ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount']) AS total_s3_gets, round(avg(ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount'])) AS avg_gets_per_query FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.query_log) WHERE event_time >= toDateTime(intDiv($__from, 1000)) AND event_time <= toDateTime(intDiv($__to, 1000)) AND type = 'QueryFinish' AND ProfileEvents['S3ReadRequestsCount'] > 0 GROUP BY source ORDER BY total_s3_gets DESC
SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards = 1

panels.title: S3 Errors — Active
panels.description: S3-related errors from system.errors. Empty = no S3 errors.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT hostName() AS node, name AS error, value AS count,
       last_error_message AS message, toDateTime(last_error_time) AS last_seen
FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.errors)
WHERE value > 0
  AND (name LIKE '%S3%' OR name LIKE '%AWS%' OR name LIKE '%Object%' OR name LIKE '%HTTP%')
SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards = 1
ORDER BY last_error_time DESC LIMIT 30

panels.title: I/O
panels.description: Hot (local) disk I/O only — file opens, compressed reads, part fetches. For S3 object storage throughput see the S3 section above.

panels.title: Open File Operations/sec
panels.description: File open syscalls per second per pod. A sudden spike can indicate a large scan or heavy compaction activity.

panels.title: Read Compressed Bytes/sec
panels.description: Compressed bytes read from local disk per second per pod.

panels.title: Read Compressed Blocks/sec
panels.description: Compressed blocks read from local disk per second per pod.

panels.title: Failed Replicated Part Fetches/sec
panels.description: Failed attempts to fetch a replicated part. Sustained failures indicate a broken replica or network issue.

panels.title: Network RX Imbalance Ratio — across Pods
panels.description: Ratio of busiest pod RX to quietest pod RX (max/min across all selected pods). 1.0 = perfectly balanced. A sustained value >2–3 means one pod is receiving disproportionately more traffic — likely a load balancer misconfiguration or a coordinator hot-spot in distributed queries.

targets.expr: max(sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_NetworkReceiveBytes{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))) / min(sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_NetworkReceiveBytes{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Total Active Parts — per Pod
panels.description: Total active MergeTree parts. A rising trend means merges are not keeping pace with inserts.

panels.title: Parts per Table — Top 20

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, count() AS active_parts, sum(rows) AS total_rows, formatReadableSize(sum(bytes_on_disk)) AS size_on_disk FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY database, table ORDER BY active_parts DESC LIMIT 20

panels.description: Active part count per table across all nodes. High counts on a specific table indicate stalled merges for that table.

panels.title: Parts per Partition — Top 20
panels.description: Partitions with the most active parts. High per-partition counts indicate merge lag within that partition.

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, partition, count() AS parts, formatReadableSize(sum(bytes_on_disk)) AS size FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY database, table, partition ORDER BY parts DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Largest Parts by Size — Top 20
panels.description: Individual parts sorted by disk size. Useful for identifying unexpectedly large parts that may slow merges.

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, name, partition, rows, formatReadableSize(bytes_on_disk) AS size_on_disk, formatReadableSize(data_uncompressed_bytes) AS size_uncompressed FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' ORDER BY bytes_on_disk DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Detached Parts — per Node
panels.description: Detached parts are excluded from queries and merges. They accumulate due to replica repair, failed fetches, or manual detach. Non-zero counts require investigation.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT hostname() AS node, database, table, reason, count() AS detached_parts FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.detached_parts) GROUP BY node, database, table, reason ORDER BY detached_parts DESC LIMIT 30
SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards = 1

panels.title: Total Active Parts — over Time
panels.description: Active MergeTree part count over time. A rising trend means merges cannot keep pace with inserts.

panels.title: Mark Cache Hit Rate — per Pod
panels.description: Fraction of mark lookups served from cache. High part counts create more unique mark ranges, pushing out cached entries. A falling hit rate alongside a rising part count is a strong sign of merge lag affecting read performance.

targets.expr:
sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_MarkCacheHits{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
/ (
  sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_MarkCacheHits{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
  + sum by (pod)(rate(ClickHouseProfileEvents_MarkCacheMisses{cluster="$cluster", pod=~"$pod"}[$__rate_interval]))
)

panels.title: Too Many Parts — Current Error State
panels.description: TOO_MANY_PARTS errors from system.errors across all nodes. Empty = no such errors — inserts are not being throttled.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT hostname() AS node, name AS error, value AS count, last_error_message AS message, toDateTime(last_error_time) AS last_seen FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.errors) WHERE name = 'TOO_MANY_PARTS' AND value > 0 ORDER BY count DESC
SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards = 1

panels.title: Oldest Active Part per Table
panels.description: Age in hours of the oldest active part per table. A very old part in a heavily written table suggests merges have stalled on that table.

targets.rawSql: SELECT database, table, max(dateDiff('hour', modification_time, now())) AS oldest_part_hours, count() AS active_parts FROM system.parts WHERE active = 1 AND database != 'system' GROUP BY database, table ORDER BY oldest_part_hours DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Pending (Inactive) Parts — per Table
panels.description: Parts with active=0 (not yet merged) across all replicas. A persistent backlog means merges cannot keep pace with inserts.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT database, table, count() AS pending_parts FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.parts) WHERE active = 0 GROUP BY database, table ORDER BY pending_parts DESC LIMIT 20
SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards = 1

panels.title: Reachable Replicas
panels.description: Count of replicas that responded to a test SQL query via clusterAllReplicas. Missing replicas indicate unreachable nodes.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count() AS reachable FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.one)
SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards = 1

panels.title: Replica Connectivity — Reachable Nodes
panels.description: Each row is a replica that successfully answered a query via clusterAllReplicas. Replicas missing from this list are unreachable from ClickHouse's perspective.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
    hostName() AS replica,
    uptime() AS uptime_sec,
    version() AS version
FROM clusterAllReplicas('default', system.one)
ORDER BY replica
SETTINGS skip_unavailable_shards = 1

panels.title: Reachable Keepers
panels.description: Number of keeper pods reachable by Prometheus. Expected: 3. Red=0, yellow=1–2, green=3. Defaults to 0 when no data.

panels.title: Cluster Disk Usage — Hot Tier
panels.description: Hot-tier disk used % across all pods. Green <70%, yellow <90%, red ≥90%. Uses DiskUsed_default / (DiskUsed_default + DiskAvailable_default).

panels.title: S3 Storage Used
panels.description: Total bytes stored in the S3 tier across all pods.

panels.title: Keeper Connectivity — per Pod
panels.description: Liveness of each keeper pod as seen by Prometheus (up=1 ALIVE, up=0 DEAD).
